findings.evidence: All stop and claim readbacks now explicitly require object.type=commit; a new adversarial test rejects non-commit refs before readSource or any mutation. Existing downstream commit/tree checks already held the stop on malformed data.

originalRecord calls validateA2Request before use; scripts/lib/patchgate-a2.mjs rejects missing/extra receipt fields and inconsistent statuses. Missing merge_commit_sha cannot bypass schema validation.

The strict receipt enum does not include merge_pending/premerge_validation_failed/postmerge_verification_in_progress. Unrecognized or transient outcomes must retain the stop; they are not proven pre-merge aborts.
A rerun can resume after an earlier completed read; revalidation before deletion prevents releasing a latch while that original run is active. Existing resumed-run test proves zero DELETE.

CLI persistIntent pushes the intent via pushReceiptCommit, fetches origin/main, reads the exact path from that ref and validates bindings. Library rejects verified=false or non-full commit. As additional hardening, remote readback now also requires identical postmerge_verification and release_intent_not_release status.

limitations: Qwen saw the complete primary function and explicit helper contracts, not all helper bytes; its review is component-scoped, not full bundle or activation approval.
